files.title: TYBBA-IB Sem V Syllabus-FINAL
files.programme: Bachelor of Business Administration in International Business (BBA-IB)

units.title: Introduction to Agribusiness Management
units.topics: 1.1 Agribusiness Management – Meaning, scope and importance of agribusiness in India, 1.2 Structure of agribusiness, 1.3 Nature and characteristics of agribusiness, 1.4 Challenges and opportunities in agribusiness, 1.5 Sustainable agriculture practices, 1.6 Contract farming, types of contract farming, 1.7 ICT in agribusiness, application of ICT in agribusiness, 1.8 Farm Planning: procedure of farm planning, 1.9 Agripreneurship and start-ups in agriculture, 1.10 Digital transformation in agriculture

units.title: Agri-Marketing and Distribution Systems
units.topics: Agri-Marketing and Distribution Systems: 2.1 Meaning and scope , importance, characteristics of agricultural products, 2.2 Distribution channels in agriculture: 2.2.1 Direct channels, 2.2.2 Indirect channels, 2.3 Supply chain management: 2.3.1 Stages of supply chain management, 2.3.2 Challenges of supply chain management

units.title: Agricultural Finance and Credit Systems
units.topics: 3.1 Meaning, nature, scope and importance of agricultural finance., 3.2 Role of agricultural finance in agribusiness and agricultural exports., 3.3 Types of agricultural credit: Short-term, medium-term, and long-term., 3.4 Sources of agricultural credit: 3.4.1 Institutional sources of credit, 3.4.2 Non-institutional: Moneylenders, traders, relatives, 3.5 Role of NABARD in rural and agricultural finance, 3.6 Government schemes and initiatives, 3.7 Microfinance and self-help groups (SHGs) in rural credit., 3.8 Export finance for agricultural products, 3.9 Issues and challenges in agricultural credit system, 3.10 Role of digital finance and fintech in agricultural lending

units.title: Agri Export and International Trade
units.topics: 4.1 Introduction to Agri Export Management, Overview of Global Agricultural Trade, 4.2 International Trade Policies and Regulations, 4.3 WTO Agreement on Agriculture (AoA), 4.4 Export Documentation and Procedures, 4.5 Terms of International Trade (Incoterms), 4.6 Export Finance and Payment Methods, 4.7 Agri Export Zones (AEZs) in India, 4.8 Role of APEDA in Agri Export Promotion, 4.9 Marketing Plan for Agri Exports

units.title: Overview of International Relations
units.topics: 1.1 Meaning, scope, objectives and principles of international relations, 1.2 Economic relations: Meaning and importance of international economic relations, international trade and global business,, 1.2.1 Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), 1.3 Legal Relations: Introduction to international law,, 1.3.1Sources of international law: Treaties, customs, international conventions, 1.3.2 Political relations: Bilateral and multilateral relations, 1.3.3 Regional political groupings: SAARC, ASEAN, BRICS, European Union

units.title: Regional Economic Integration & Current Practices
units.topics: 2.1 European Union (EU) & their current practices; Brexit its reasons and implications., 2.2 North Atlantic Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) & their current Practices, 2.3 South Asian Association for Regional Co -operation (SAARC) & their current Practices, 2.4 SAARC Preferential Trading Arrangement (SAPTA) & their current Practices, 2.5 Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa (BRICS), 2.6 India’s Role in Regional Economic Integration and Recent Global Trade Developments.

units.title: International Trade Governance and Legal Challenges
units.topics: 3.1 WTO provisions relating to preferential treatment of developing Countries, 3.2 Implications of WTO pertaining to: 3.2.1 General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS), Trade Related Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPs), Trade Related Investment measures (TRIMs), commodity agreement., 3.2.5 India’s foreign trade policy and recent trade reforms, 3.2.6 International trade challenges and emerging business environment

units.title: Social and Trade Relations in Global Business
units.topics: 4.1 Social structure, diversity, and inclusive growth, 4.2 Culture and workplace environment, 4.3 Cultural sensitivity and global business adaptation, 4.4 Trade policy instruments and government regulations: 4.4.1 Tariffs and non-tariff barriers, 4.4.2 Subsidies and export promotion measures, 4.4.3 Quotas and trade restrictions, 4.5 Dumping, fair-trade practices, and trade protection measures, 4.6 Contemporary issues in geopolitical conflict

units.title: Introduction to Management Information Systems (MIS)
units.topics: 1.1 Definition, Concepts, and Evolution of MIS, 1.2 Role and Significance of MIS in Modern Business, 1.3 Components of MIS: Hardware, Software, Data, People, Procedures, 1.4 Structure and Classification of MIS (Operational, Tactical, Strategic levels), 1.5 Difference between Data, Information, and Knowledge, 1.6 MIS and Corporate Strategy: Achieving Competitive Advantage

units.title: Decision Support Systems and Business Analytics
units.topics: 2.1 Managerial decision-making process, 2.2 Types of decisions: Structured, semi-structured, and unstructured decisions, 2.3 Concepts and components of Decision Support Systems (DSS), 2.4 Executive Support Systems (ESS) and Group Decision Support Systems (GDSS), 2.5 Introduction to Business Intelligence (BI) and Business Analytics (BA), 2.6 Application of Data Mining, Big Data, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in decision-making

units.title: Enterprise Applications and Functional Information Systems
units.topics: 3.1 Overview of Enterprise Systems: Meaning, Architecture, and Benefits, 3.2 Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP): Implementation, advantages, and challenges, 3.3 Customer Relationship Management (CRM) Systems, 3.4 Supply Chain Management (SCM) Systems, 3.5 Functional Information Systems: Marketing, Human Resource, Financial, and Production Information Systems, 3.6 Cloud computing and SaaS models in enterprise systems

units.title: Emerging Trends and Ethical Issues in MIS
units.topics: 4.1 Recent Trends: Mobile computing, Internet of Things (IoT), and Blockchain in MIS, 4.2 Information Security Concepts: Threats, vulnerabilities, and cyber security management, 4.3 Disaster Recovery and Business Continuity Planning, 4.4 Ethical and Social Issues in Information Systems: Privacy, data protection, and intellectual property rights, 4.5 IT Act and cyber laws in India (Overview)

units.title: Introduction to Production and Operations Management
units.topics: 1.1 Introduction, Meaning, Definition and Scope of Production Management, 1.2 Nature of Production Management, 1.3 Operations Management - Meaning, Definition and Scope, 1.4 Distinction between Manufacturing and Service Operations, 1.5 Objectives of Operations Management, 1.6 Continuous System (Mass, Flow, Process), 1.7 Intermittent System (Batch, Job-Shop, Project), 1.8 Factors affecting system selection

units.title: Materials and Maintenance Management
units.topics: 2.1 Introduction, ddefinitions and scope of materials management, 2.2 Material handling principles and practices, 2.3 Criteria for selection of materials, material handling equipment, standardization, codification and simplification, 2.4 Inventory Management - Meaning, types of inventory, 2.5 Techniques of Inventory Management - ABC Analysis, EOQ, VED, Safety Stock, JIT, 2.6 Maintenance Management: Objectives, Types: Preventive, Breakdown, Predictive, Routine

units.title: Quality Management and Control
units.topics: 3.1 Meaning, concept and dimensions of quality, 3.2 Total Quality Management (TQM) - Principles and Implementation, 3.3 Quality Control (QC) and Quality Assurance (QA) - Concepts and distinction, 3.4 Statistical Quality Control (SQC) - Control charts for variables and attributes, 3.5 Six Sigma - Concepts, Methodology (DMAIC), benefits, 3.6 Quality Standards - ISO 9000 series, ISO 14000, 3.7 Continuous Improvement Tools - Kaizen, 5S, Kanban, Poka-Yoke

units.title: Industrial Safety and Waste Management
units.topics: 4.1 Meaning, importance, and legal aspects of industrial safety (Factories Act provisions), 4.2 Types of industrial hazards: Mechanical, chemical, electrical, and fire hazards, 4.3 Safety measures, accident prevention, and personal protective equipment (PPE), 4.4 Ergonomics in workplace safety, 4.5 Concepts, types of industrial waste (solid, liquid, hazardous), 4.6 Waste minimization techniques (3Rs: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle), 4.7 Environmental management systems and pollution control standards

units.title: Introduction to Industrial Marketing
units.topics: 1.1 Meaning, definition, and nature of Industrial (B2B) Marketing, 1.2 Scope and importance of Industrial Marketing, 1.3 Differences between Industrial Marketing and Consumer (B2C) Marketing, 1.4 Characteristics of industrial markets, 1.5 Types of industrial customers: Commercial enterprises, Government organizations, and Institutions, 1.6 Industrial product classification: Materials and parts, Capital items, Operating supplies and services, 1.7 Emerging trends in Business-to-Business (B2B) marketing

units.title: Industrial Buying Behaviour
units.topics: 2.1 Understanding industrial customers and buying situations (Straight Rebuy, Modified Rebuy, New Task), 2.2 The Buying Center concept: Roles and influence of buying center members, 2.3 Industrial buying process: Step-by-step model of organizational decision-making, 2.4.4 Factors influencing industrial buying behaviour

units.title: Market Segmentation, Pricing, Promotion and Distribution Strategies
units.topics: 3.1 Meaning and bases of B2B market segmentation: Macro and micro segmentation, 3.2 Target marketing and product positioning strategies in industrial markets, 3.3 Pricing in Industrial Marketing: Factors influencing industrial pricing decisions, 3.4 Pricing strategies: Competitive bidding, negotiated pricing, leasing, and value-based pricing, 3.5 Role of direct and indirect channels in B2B marketing, 3.6 Channel selection, management, and evaluation of industrial intermediaries, 3.7 Industrial Promotion Mix: Role of personal selling in industrial markets, 3.8 Trade shows, exhibitions, catalogues, and direct marketing, 3.9 Relationship marketing and Key Account Management (KAM)

units.title: Recent Trends in Industrial Marketing
units.topics: 4.1 Digital marketing in B2B: Content marketing, search engine optimization (SEO), and LinkedIn marketing, 4.2 Role of e-procurement and digital marketplaces in industrial transactions, 4.3 Customer Relationship Management (CRM) in industrial marketing, 4.4 Supply chain integration and customer value co-creation, 4.5 Sustainability and green practices in industrial marketing, 4.6 Global business-to-business marketing: Opportunities and challenges

units.title: Introduction to Financial Services
units.topics: 1.1 Meaning and Concept of Financial Services. 1.2 Features of Financial Services. 1.3 Types of Financial Services: - Fund Based & Fee Based. 1.4 Importance of Financial Services. 1.5 Challenges to Financial Service Sector. 1.6 Present Scenario of Financial Services in India.

units.title: Fund Based Financial Services
units.topics: 2.1 Meaning and Concept of Hire Purchase, Features of Hire Purchase, Process of Hire Purchase. 2.2 Meaning and Concept of Leasing, Features of Leasing, Process of Leasing. 2.3 Difference between Hire Purchase and Leasing. 2.4 Meaning and Concept of Factoring, Mechanism of Factoring, Types of Factoring. 2.5 Meaning and Concept of Forfeiting, Mechanism of Forfeiting. 2.6 Difference between Factoring and Forfeiting.

units.title: Fee Based Financial Services
units.topics: 3.1 Merchant Banking: - Meaning, Definition, Scope, Functions, Stages of Merchant Banking. 3.2 Credit Rating: - Meaning, Concept, Functions, Credit Rating Agencies in India: CRISIL, ICRA, CARE. 3.3 Securitization: - Meaning, Concept, Process, Advantages, Stages of Securitization. 3.4 Stock Broking: - Meaning, Concept, Functions, Types of Stock Brokers.

units.title: Financial Market and Financial Services
units.topics: 3.1 Meaning and Concept of Financial Market. 3.2 Features and Functions of Financial Market. 3.3 Types of Financial Markets & Financial Instruments: - Money Market, Capital Market, Foreign Exchange Market, Credit Market. 3.4 Meaning and Concept of Mutual Funds, Types of Mutual Funds, Portfolio Management Services (PMS): Types of PMS, Advantages of PMS. 3.5 Venture Capital: - Meaning and Concept, Features, Stages of Venture Capital Financing. 3.6 Private Equity: - Meaning, Concept, Stages of Private Equity.

units.title: Introduction to International Economics
units.topics: 1.1 Meaning, nature and scope of international economics, 1.2 Distinction between internal and international trade, 1.3 Importance of international economics, 1.4 Theories of International Trade: 1.4.1 Mercantilist views on trade, 1.4.2 Adam Smith’s theory of Absolute Cost Advantage, 1.4.3 David Ricardo’s theory of Comparative Cost Advantage, 1.4.4 Heckscher-Ohlin (H-O) Theory of International Trade

units.title: Terms of Trade and Balance of payment
units.topics: 2.1 Meaning and types of terms of trade: 2.1.1 Factors affecting terms of trade, 2.1.2 Gains from international trade, 2.1.3 Trade as an engine of economic growth, 2.2 Balance of Payments (BOP): 2.2.1 Meaning and structure of Balance of Payments, 2.2.2 Distinction between Balance of Trade and Balance of Payments, 2.2.3 Causes of disequilibrium in Balance of Payments, 2.2.4 Measures to correct BOP disequilibrium, 2.2.5 Recent trends in India’s Balance of Payments

units.title: Entrepreneurship Fundamentals
units.topics: 1.1 Meaning and concept, attributes and mind -set of entrepreneurial and intrapreneurial leadership, role models in each and their role in economic development., 1.2 Understanding and analyzing the macro-Problem and Industry perspective, technological, socio economic and urbanization trends and their implication on new opportunities., 1.3 Aligning passion, identifying and defining problem using design thinking principles, analyzing problem and validating with the potential customer.

units.title: Customer Discovery, Ideation and competition mapping
units.topics: 2.1 Understanding customer, customer segmentation, creating and validating customer personas., 2.2 Understanding Customer Jobs -to-be-done and crafting innovative solution design to map to customer’s needs and create a strong value proposition. Iterating problem-customer fit., 2.3 Examining ideation techniques and generating solution ideas. Competition and Industry trends mapping for assessing market sizing - initial opportunity.

units.title: Field Visit Structure
units.topics: Pre-visit orientation session by concerned teachers, Selection of industry/organization (department level), Visit to manufacturing firms / service organisations / logistics companies/ Export houses, Interaction with professionals, Data collection and observation (Preparing Questionnaire

units.title: Student Activities During Visit
units.topics: Follow discipline (safety protocols) as prescribed by the organization., Observation of business operations for practical understanding, Interaction with officials, Documentation study (if any), Understanding working of business firms, Note-taking and data collection, Photography (if permitted)

units.title: Project preparation
units.topics: The final project shall be presented as a book along with a presentation to be evaluated by the faculty mentor.

units.title: Field Visit Report Format
units.topics: 1. Title page, 2. Certificate, 3. Acknowledgement, 4. Objectives of Visit, 5. Company/Organization Profile, 6. Methodology, 7. Observations and findings, 8. Learning Outcomes, 9. Conclusion, 10. References, 11. Annexures (photos, brochures, etc.)
